UAE says Iran targeted ADNOC tanker in Strait of Hormuz, no casualties (Al Jazeera, Sat 8 Aug 2026)

The United Arab Emirates on Saturday said Iran had targeted a tanker belonging to the state-owned Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (ADNOC) while it was transiting the Strait of Hormuz.

UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs statement: condemned "a hostile Iranian attack that targeted a tanker belonging to ADNOC with a missile while it was transiting the Strait of Hormuz, without causing casualties." Described the strike as "an act of piracy by Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC)." Called on Tehran to "halt the attacks and reopen the strait fully and unconditionally." Said the attack was a flagrant violation of UN Security Council Resolution 2817, which affirms freedom of navigation.

ADNOC statement (issued Friday, restated Sat): since the start of the war, 15 of its vessels had been attacked by missiles and drones while transiting the strait, "including three this week alone" — killing one crew member and injuring 20 others. Company said it is operating in an "exceptionally challenging environment."

Regional condemnations Saturday:
- GCC Secretary-General Jassim Mohammed al-Budaiwi: called the attack a "dangerous and unacceptable escalation," calling for international action to protect maritime navigation.
- Qatar: rejected using the Strait as "a bargaining chip."
- Saudi Arabia: condemned the targeting "in the strongest terms," citing violation of international law and Resolution 2817.
- Jordan: called it "a flagrant violation of international law."

Context: Since the US-Israeli war on Iran broke out on 28 February, shipping has been repeatedly disrupted. About a fifth of the world's oil and LNG passed through the strait prior to the conflict.
